column1: # Seed keywords: Iraq, the Kurdistan Region, the governorates and their main cities.
# Public place and national names only (plan §5.1, §8.10). Brand, person and topic
# keywords are entered in the database and never committed to this public repo.
#   group      the governorate a place belongs to; "iraq" for country-level names,
#   kind       what the keyword names; every row here is "place" (plan §5.1 kinds:
#   lang       languages the variants cover, comma-separated:
#                en  = English and other common Latin transliterations
#   ambiguous  1 if the spellings are also common words, people's names, brands or
#              other places, so a match needs another Iraq signal; otherwise 0
#   variants   spellings separated by "|". They are normalized before matching
#              (see Normalize), so accents, hamza forms and ة/ه differences do not
#              need separate entries. Matching is whole-word.
#   - One row per place. A spelling shared by several languages is listed once.
#   - "<id>-ambiguous" holds the spellings of an otherwise clear name that collide with
#     a common word or another name in one language. Examples: Turkish "Bağdat" is also
#     a well-known Istanbul avenue; Arabic "الرمادي" also means "the grey"; Arabic
#   - "<id>-governorate" holds "X Governorate" phrases for governorates whose bare name
#     is ambiguous. The phrase itself is clear.
#   - Kurmanji oblique forms ending in -ê (for example "Hewlêrê", "in Erbil") are listed
#     because they are common in running text and matching is whole-word.
#   - Halabja is included as a governorate; the Kurdistan Region lists it as one.

column6: إقليم كردستان|إقليم كوردستان|إقليم كردستان العراق|إقليم كوردستان العراق|كردستان العراق|كوردستان العراق|هەرێمی کوردستان|هەرێمی کوردستانی عێراق|کوردستانی عێراق|باشووری کوردستان|Herêma Kurdistanê|Başûrê Kurdistanê|Kurdistana Başûr|Kurdistan Region|Iraqi Kurdistan|Kürdistan Bölgesi|Irak Kürdistanı

column1: # Sulaymaniyah. Arabic "السليمانية" is also a district of Riyadh and the Süleymaniye
# Mosque; after normalization Sorani "سلێمانی" and Kurmanji "Silêmanî" equal the
# surname Soleimani; Turkish "Süleymaniye" is usually the Istanbul mosque.
# Babil and Hillah. "Babil"/"Babylon" is also the ancient city, a common brand and
# a film/TV title. Arabic "الحلة" is also "the outfit" and, in Gulf Arabic, "the pot".

column6: محافظة بابل|پارێزگای بابل|Babil Governorate|Babylon Governorate|Babil Province|Babylon Province

column1: # Wasit and Kut. Arabic "واسط" also means "middle"/"go-between". "Kut"/"الكوت" is
# also a Turkic word and surname, Iraqi slang for "coat", and a Dutch swear word.

column6: محافظة واسط|پارێزگای واست|پارێزگای واسیت|Wasit Governorate|Wasit Province

column1: # Maysan and Amarah. Arabic "العمارة" also means "the building"/"architecture";
# Dhi Qar and Nasiriyah. Arabic "الناصرية" is also "Nasserism".
# Muthanna and Samawah. "المثنى" is also a given name and the Arabic grammatical dual.
# Al-Qadisiyyah and Diwaniyah. "القادسية" is also a historic battle and the name of
# several sports clubs. Arabic "الديوانية" is also a Gulf reception hall (diwaniya).

column6: محافظة القادسية|پارێزگای قادسیە|Qadisiyyah Governorate|Qadisiyah Governorate|Qadisiyyah Province|Qadisiyah Province

column1: # Saladin, Tikrit and Samarra. "Saladin"/"صلاح الدين" is also the historical figure
# and a very common given name.

column6: محافظة صلاح الدين|پارێزگای سەلاحەدین|Saladin Governorate|Salahuddin Governorate|Salah al-Din Governorate|Saladin Province|Salahuddin Province|Salah al-Din Province
